item.name: POST createFromTemplate — slug uniqueness is ORG-WIDE, so a different name/owner does not unlock it

request.description:
Retries the taken slug with a DIFFERENT app name, pinning that the collision is decided by the slug alone.

⚠️ THIS REQUEST USED TO ASSERT THE OPPOSITE, AND IT ASSERTED SOMETHING NOTHING IMPLEMENTS. It read 'different user + same slug → 201 (cross-user reuse OK)' and cited 'REQ-OBTC-004 owner-scoped uniqueness'. Three things were wrong with that:

1. REQ-OBTC-004 says the opposite. Its only slug scenario — openspec/specs/openbuild-template-catalogue/spec.md:254-261 — is 'Clone with an existing slug is rejected … a slug that matches an existing Application IN THEIR ORGANISATION → 4xx'. There is no owner-scoped uniqueness anywhere in the spec.
2. The product deliberately scopes org-wide. ApplicationsController:1467-1478 carries the comment 'Slug uniqueness org-wide (no owner filter) to prevent squatting' and pointedly does NOT pass lookupOne()'s optional $owner argument.
3. The 'different user' never existed. {{second_user}} (`tester`) is created by neither tests/e2e/ci-seed.sh nor tests/e2e/global-setup.ts, and a per-request Basic override cannot switch users anyway once Newman holds a session cookie for the origin (server/lib/base.php:1054-1066). The request ran as admin — and createFromTemplate is admin-only (ApplicationsController:1377-1383), so a genuinely-authenticated `tester` would have got 403, never 201.

So it was red because it demanded behaviour that the spec forbids, the code refuses, and its own premise could not be established. It now asserts the contract that is actually specified.
